Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: C
Q2: B

RATIONALE:
Q1: This issue's body has no `Integration branch:` or `Target branch:` line, so `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` (lines 15 and 28) sends the work to the default branch, `main`. Nothing in the triage body changes that. The implementer works on a `main` checkout and cannot check out PR #6649's head. So the work happens on `main`, and code changes only if the failing tests also fail on `main`. If they fail only on #6649's head, the defect belongs to PR #6649, and its own review/autofix loop already receives its failed checks (`CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED`). A `main` PR would not turn that check green.
Q2: The failed shard's test list can be rebuilt exactly from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, without the missing log. Re-running that list a few times costs little and catches intermittent failures, which are real defects worth fixing. If every run passes, close with no code change. Option C is excluded: it edits a workflow file without a `files_touched` grant and does not address the failure.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines ~1290-1333 (fast-fail / remaining split that writes `/tmp/orchestrate_poll_remaining_tests.txt`), 1371-1398 (group and shard partition)
    - `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`
    - `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`
  steps:
    - On the default-branch checkout, rebuild the remaining-tests list with the same Python block CI uses (ci.yml ~1290-1333).
    - Build the failed shard's list. Take group 3 of 4: `awk -v n=3 -v total=4 'NR % total == n'` on the remaining list. Then take shard 1 of 4 from that: `awk -v n=1 -v total=4 'NR % total == n'`.
    - Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py <those tests>`.
    - If any test fails, fix the root cause in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` or the test fixture, whichever the failure points to. Keep the change minimal.
    - If all pass, go to the Q2 path. Do not open a `main` PR that only guesses at PR #6649's change.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "fix the branch where the check failed" becomes "fix on the default branch only when the failure reproduces there".
  equivalence_argument: A defect on `main` gets fixed on `main`, and #6649 picks it up when it merges from `main`. A defect only on #6649's head is already in that PR's review/autofix loop, which reads its failed checks.
  reversibility: A human can add `Target branch: ai/issue-6642` to this issue body and run `/reclarify` to send the work to the PR branch.
Q2:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - the shard-1 / group-3 test list from Q1
  steps:
    - Run that list 3 times in a row (bounded so it fits the 60-minute budget).
    - Run it once more alongside the other three shards of group 3 at the same time, as CI does.
    - If any run fails, fix the cause of the intermittent failure, for example shared tempdir or state, or ordering. Do not loosen any assertion or the gate in ci.yml 1416-1443.
    - If every run passes, make no code change. Report it as not reproducible on the default branch, list the tests that were run, and say the fix (if any) belongs to PR #6649's own review loop or a CI re-run of #6649.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "identify the failing test from the full job log" becomes "identify it by rebuilding the shard list deterministically and running it again".
  equivalence_argument: The shard partition is deterministic `NR % total` over a fixed list, so the rebuilt list is exactly the set of tests the failed shard ran.
  reversibility: If a human later has the full log showing a test that fails only on #6649's head, the fix goes to PR #6649. No change is made on `main` in that case.
